lockup.summary: The company, its officers, directors and holders of nearly all its stock cannot sell for 180 days after the prospectus date without the lead banks' written consent. The banks say they do not plan to release any shares early.

what: It develops RNA-based medicines called siRNA drugs to treat many diseases, with three in human trials.
proceeds: It expects about $408.1 million from the offering and $87.2 million from a private sale to AbbVie. It plans about $180 million for agazisiran, $65 million for onvuzosiran, $80 million for ADX-626, $25 million for ADX-077 and $20 million for ADX-199, with the rest for research and general costs.
risks: It is a young company with no approved products and has not finished any clinical program, so its future is hard to judge.
It expects to keep losing money for the foreseeable future and may never become profitable.
Even after this offering it will need much more money, which could dilute shareholders or force it to cut research programs.
